free_tier.stated: Up to 100 buckets, each up to 100 TB / 50 million objects; 5 TB max per object; regions FSN1/HEL1/NBG1

egress.terms: the base price includes 1 TB of egress a month for the whole account, accumulated hourly (at most 1.1160 TB in a 31-day month) and not carried over to the next month; ingress, internal traffic within the eu-central network zone and S3 operations such as PUT, GET and DELETE are free, but the egress those operations cause is billed
egress.price_per_tb: EUR 1.0000 per TB beyond the included quota, excl. VAT

tooling: AWS CLI, rclone, all S3 SDKs
chaining: S3 origin; internal traffic within the eu-central network zone is free of charge, so a Hetzner Cloud server in that zone reads the buckets without egress charges

limits.value: 750 requests/s per source IP and 750 requests/s per bucket
256 active parallel TCP sessions per source IP
100 TB and 50 million objects per bucket, up to 100 buckets per account

limits_note: billed for every hour at least one bucket exists, even if empty; minimum billable object size 64 kB; 10 Gbit/s per bucket for reads or writes; 5 GB per single PUT and per multipart part, up to 10,000 parts; 8 kB of metadata per object

identity_cost.detail: before an order is processed the account may have to be verified with a copy of a valid government-issued ID (ID card or passport) or with an advance payment from the holder's own credit card; registrants are asked not to use a free email address or a VPN service

reliability_note: LowEndTalk scepticism: "bandwidth limit is per bucket (not per object) and the pricing is based on 1TB increments it makes feel that it's just a fancy wrapped single-node storage with S3 compatibility, rather than actual distributed object storage".
confidence_note: The page states the number in the record; the claim is documented, not measured.
